transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-07 14:30 PDT | Duration: 42 min | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Leo Vargas (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (CTO), Sofia Gomez (Lead ML), Ethan Moore (Security)

Auto-generated summary: Bluefield is evaluating Redwood for a hybrid rollout — start with PLG/self-serve hosted API for rapid prototyping with free credits, then evaluate Dedicated/reserved or VPC/private for regulated datasets. Key concerns: data residency, KMS integration, SSO, and predictable latency/costs. Agreed next steps include sending quickstart materials, scheduling an SE deep-dive, and sharing a set of sample prompts for a benchmark.

Topics: quickstart & credits; time-to-first-token (TTFT); hosted vs dedicated vs private; security (SOC2, SAML, KMS); latency vs cost tradeoffs; pilot criteria and success metrics.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick intro — maya from Redwood, leo our solutions engineer is with me. how are you all?
[00:07] Ravi: doing well, thanks. thanks for taking this. we're excited — Bluefield is looking to add llm features to our analytics workspace.
[00:12] Maya: great. goal for today is to understand your timeline, constraints, and see if the self-serve quickstart with credits gets you to a first token quickly, or if we should look at dedicated / private options.
[00:23] Sofia: main thing for us is time-to-first-token. we want engineers to ship an internal prototype in two weeks. second, our security team will want to know about data residency and key management.
[00:31] Leo: totally. for the TTFT path we usually recommend the hosted redis — sorry the hosted api path, plg flow: sign up, we give credits, quickstart sdk, you run a sample generation. typically teams hit first token in under an hour if they follow the quickstart.
[00:45] Ethan: yeah, that sounds good. for security we have SOC two requirements and we need to enforce SSO/SAML and customer-managed keys ideally. do you support KMS / HSM?
[00:55] Leo: yes. our hosted product supports customer-managed encryption keys via KMS integrations and we have enterprise plans with HSM support — in private or dedicated deployments we can also integrate with on-prem HSM. note: automated audit logs and token-level tracing are available on the console.
[01:12] Ravi: what about data residency? some of our customers are EU-based and we need to ensure data doesn't leave region.
[01:18] Maya: we have regional hosting options in EU and NA, and for stricter needs the Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) is the path. if you start hosted for prototyping, you can later pin to a dedicated/reserved pool in the EU region for production.
[01:31] Sofia: curious about cost — what's the typical delta between hosted and dedicated? and how does batching/kv caching affect unit costs?
[01:39] Leo: good question. hosted is pay-as-you-go; dedicated offers a lower per-token cost via committed capacity. caching and continuous batching can drop effective per-token cost a lot for repeat prefixes. we can share model/sample profiles that show expected cost curves once we know your QPS and prompt distribution.
[01:55] (brief cross-talk)
[02:00] Ethan: any concerns with latency? our product has interactive components — sub-400ms tail is ideal for end-user flows.
[02:08] Leo: sub-400ms is attainable for shorter context lengths on lighter models. for strict SLAs we recommend dedicated pools or local private inference. hosted has SLOs but if you need consistent latency guarantees, dedicated with reserved GPUs will be the most predictable. we can run a benchmark as part of the pilot.
[02:27] Ravi: sounds good. for the pilot, can we do hosted first with credits and then measure and move to dedicated if needed?
[02:32] Maya: yes that's our typical path. we'll provision credits for a sandbox workspace so your devs can prototype. if the metrics indicate we need dedicated, we can scope a reserved pool.
[02:40] Sofia: ok walk me through what a dev needs to do to hit first token — I want to remove friction.
[02:45] Leo: step one: sign up and confirm email. step two: we give a quickstart token and example repo — we have SDK snippets for JS/Python and a curl example. step three: run a simple completion example or embedding call. replace the sample prompt with your prompt set. usually ~30–60 minutes.
[03:05] Maya: also we'll share a short playbook: configuring batching, prefix caching, and selecting model family. link: https://redwood.example/quickstart-playbook (shared).
[03:15] Ravi: perfect. on the security docs, can you send SOC two report and the architecture for private deployments?
[03:21] Maya: yes — i'll attach our security pack (SOC2 report, pen test summary, data flow diagrams). for private we have a VPC connector doc and an on-prem install spec.
[03:32] Ethan: how intrusive is the VPC connector? we prefer minimal network changes.
[03:36] Leo: the connector sits as an egress/ingress path using customer-managed routing; typically networking teams open a couple of outbound ports and we set up a secure tunnel. for full air-gapped on-prem, that's a slightly bigger program but doable.
[03:51] Sofia: any gotchas with model compatibility — we're currently prototyping with an open decoder model. do you host many models and will the SDK calls change?
[03:58] Leo: SDK calls are consistent across models and deployments. we maintain a model catalog — the call shape is the same, you only change model identifier and some params. note: some older model archs have different kv cache behaviour but runtime handles it in most cases.
[04:14] Ravi: good. timeline — we want prototype in two weeks and a pilot in four to six weeks. is that realistic?
[04:20] Maya: yes. proto in two weeks is totally reasonable via hosted quickstart. pilot for performance and privacy in 4–6 weeks is also feasible if we get sample prompts and QPS this week.
[04:29] (pause)
[04:32] Ethan: about compliance — we may need contractual language about retention and deletion. can you support explicit retention windows and customer-controlled deletion?
[04:39] Maya: yes we can support configurable retention and can add contractual terms for data deletion and retention windows for enterprise deals.
[04:46] Sofia: what's the process to move from hosted to dedicated? do we need to change endpoints or is it seamless?
[04:51] Leo: it's mostly config: you can pin a route to a dedicated model variant and the endpoint remains the same if you use our routing abstractions. in practice we provide a migration plan and can do a canary rollout.
[05:04] Ravi: ok, what about cost for a small dedicated pool? ballpark numbers?
[05:09] Maya: i'll send ballpark pricing in the follow-up — depends on model family and throughput. for a small reserved pool expect a monthly commit; we have examples in the pricing sheet.
[05:20] (several minutes of clarifying questions — transcription gets fuzzy)
[10:12] Maya: quick note — for the TTFT playbook I'll include a curated minimal prompt set and example SDK snippet targeted at your stack.
[10:19] Sofia: great. also we'd like a live demo where the SE runs a benchmark with our prompts — can that be scheduled next week?
[10:25] Leo: yes, i'll set up a 60-minute session. we'll do a baseline on hosted then iterate with caching and batch config to show cost/latency tradeoffs.
[10:33] Ethan: please include audit logging and KMS integration steps in the doc so our security folks can review.
[10:38] Maya: will do.
[10:41] Ravi: any concerns around vendor lock-in? we prefer portable integration if we need to move later.
[10:46] Leo: our SDK and API follow open-ish patterns; we encourage exporting prompts and KV caches aren't portable but model and prompt assets are. we'll discuss fallback policies and export options in the deep-dive.
[10:58] Maya: ok to recap — action items: maya send quickstart + security pack + credits; leo schedule technical deep-dive + prepare perf checklist; sofia to share prompts and expected traffic.
[11:12] Sofia: yes i'll share the prompt set and a spreadsheet with traffic estimates.
[11:18] Ethan: i'll sync with procurement about contract terms around retention and bring any questions to the next call.
[11:24] Maya: awesome. any final Qs?
[11:26] Ravi: none here, thanks.
[11:29] Maya: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the links and proposed times.
[11:33] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: minor mis-hearings around acronyms (SOC two vs SOC 2), occasional speaker swaps around minutes 05–10 when several people overlap.

Referenced artifacts / links: https://redwood.example/quickstart-playbook, https://redwood.example/security-pack, shared spreadsheet: bluefield-sample-prompts.xlsx (customer to provide).

Pilot success criteria (spoken):
- Prototype within 2 weeks (internal demo)
- Baseline latency under target (sub-400ms median for interactive flows) or clear migration path to dedicated pool
- Cost-per-call estimates within budget envelope after caching/batching optimizations
- Security: SOC2 evidence, SSO/SAML support, KMS integration confirmed

End of transcript.
